question: What is the most reliable, go-to test used in labs to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?

options.C: Nucleic acid amplification testing
options.D: Complete blood cell count analysis

question: Why do fat-soluble hormones need carrier proteins to travel in the blood?

options.A: Carrier proteins are needed to digest the hormone
options.B: They do not mix well with the watery plasma
options.C: They are too heavy to float without assistance
options.D: They would instantly destroy red blood cells if free

explanation: Oil and water don't mix! Since fat-soluble hormones don't dissolve in watery blood plasma, they need special carrier proteins to give them a ride through the circulatory system. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the most frequent cause of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)?

options.A: Severe iodine deficiency

question: How do people usually catch an Ascaris infection?

question: Why must a community health nurse be versatile and take on multiple roles like educator, manager, and clinician?

options.A: To ensure that administrative paperwork takes up the entire workday
options.B: To effectively address the wide variety of health and social needs in a population
options.C: To avoid working with community leaders and traditional health practitioners
options.D: To replace local doctors in diagnosing and performing major surgeries

explanation: Because community settings present complex social and health problems, nurses must switch between teaching, managing, and direct care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h2)

question: Why is checking out the home environment so important for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will eat all prescribed meals
options.B: It reveals practical barriers like trouble with grocery shopping
options.C: It proves whether the family is hiding food from the patient
options.D: It replaces the need to check the patient's weight

explanation: Exactly! Home visits show you real-life challenges, like physical issues that make buying or cooking food hard. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why are cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, which drops their white blood cell count, so prone to infections?

options.A: Their body temperature drops below the minimum required for normal cellular survival
options.B: Their stomach stops producing the acid required to digest nutrients
options.C: They lose the cellular defense tools needed to identify and destroy invading microorganisms
options.D: Their skin immediately loses its elasticity and tears open from minimal pressure

explanation: Correct! Chemotherapy slows down bone marrow production, leaving white blood cells too low to properly fight off everyday germs. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T4#GNS313_U1_T4_h3)

question: When should a community health nurse clean and disinfect a measuring tape?

options.A: Only when it looks visibly dirty
options.B: Once a month during equipment audit
options.C: At the end of each working week
options.D: After every single client use

explanation: Wiping the tape after every patient prevents the spread of skin infections and pathogens between community members. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h6)

question: When should a nurse avoid giving medications by the oral route?

options.A: When the drug is prescribed in liquid form
options.B: When the patient is eating a normal meal
options.C: When the patient has a mild headache
options.D: When the patient is vomiting or unconscious

question: What is a major warning sign that a newborn is struggling to make the normal transition to baby circulation?

options.B: Persistent central cyanosis
options.C: Excessive weight gain on day one
options.D: Frequent passing of meconium

question: How does long-term release of cortisol help the body cope with extended stress?

options.A: By increasing available blood glucose and energy supplies
options.B: By lowering the heart rate and blood pressure to rest
options.C: By promoting rapid storage of extra body fat in muscles
options.D: By enhancing digestion and nutrient absorption in the gut

explanation: Cortisol breaks down stored fats and proteins to keep your blood sugar up, ensuring your body has plenty of energy to push through tough, stressful times. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why do many pregnant women experience mild shortness of breath during normal daily activities?

options.C: Airways narrow due to chronic allergic reactions in pregnancy.
options.D: Red blood cell production suddenly drops to dangerously low levels.

question: Which vitamin is often given alongside isoniazid to protect a patient's nerves?

options.A: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3)

options.C: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
options.D: Tocopherol (Vitamin E)

explanation: Isoniazid can drain Vitamin B6 levels, leading to tingling or nerve pain. Adding Vitamin B6 prevents this pesky side effect. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h7)

question: Your patient scheduled for a liver biopsy says they just took their morning dose of warfarin (a blood thinner). What should you do?

options.A: Tell them to walk around the ward to sweat it out

options.C: Inform the doctor immediately and expect the test to be delayed

question: A patient with psychomotor seizures has a history of a severe car accident two years ago. What is the most likely cause?

options.B: Degenerative autoimmune decline
options.C: Congenital metabolic defect
options.D: Primary brain tumor growth

question: When is ibuprofen unsafe to use for fever in a child?

options.C: When the child has concurrent dehydration or kidney issues
options.D: When the child has a mild ear infection

question: What type of energy does an MRI machine use to take pictures of inside the body?

question: What is the main reason hospitals require strict paperwork when disposing of damaged or expired drugs?

options.C: To ensure pharmaceutical companies pay for the hospital water bills

question: Why does a crashing patient make standard IV drug delivery so difficult?

question: Which group of people is most at risk of sudden, severe dehydration from diarrhea?

question: How do major community accidents immediately affect local hospitals and clinics?

options.D: By increasing the number of available nurses on duty

question: What main chemical messenger is released by parasympathetic nerves during sexual arousal?

question: What is an effective way for a nurse to start talking about loss with a patient?

question: What is the main goal of doing a mental status examination during a home visit?

question: What is the main difference between mechanical and chemical digestion?

question: Which client is the best choice for a progestin-only contraceptive method?

question: Why is food safety such a big priority for community health nurses?

question: What is the main goal of community programs that prevent adolescent substance use?

question: A grand multiparous woman arrives at the labor ward in active labor. What is the very first priority action you should take as the nurse?

question: A mother brings her young child with sickle cell anaemia to the clinic. Which statement by the mother shows she understands home care instructions?

question: What is the main reason for putting a Plaster of Paris cast on a broken bone?

question: Why do we reference sources in nursing writing?

question: Which of these is a direct legal duty for a nurse administrator?

question: Poor waste disposal and unsafe drinking water lead directly to which group of diseases?

options.B: It stops the tumor from spreading to other organs

options.D: It creates new blood vessels to supply oxygen and nutrients

explanation: Clever! Tumors need food and oxygen to keep growing rapidly. By triggering angiogenesis, they force the body to build a dedicated supply line straight to them. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h3)

question: What do we call health issues that linger for weeks or months after recovering from COVID-19?

options.A: Acute rebound syndrome
options.B: Secondary convalescence
options.C: Long COVID
options.D: Delayed viral shedding

explanation: When symptoms stick around long after the initial infection is gone, it's known as Long COVID. You're making steady progress! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is the absolute heart of therapeutic communication in nursing?

options.A: Talking more than the patient talks
options.B: Giving immediate personal advice
options.C: Changing the subject when it gets sad
options.D: Active listening without judgment

explanation: Patients open up when they feel heard and safe. Listening without judging them builds instant trust. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is advocating for good patient nutrition such a big deal in modern nursing?

options.A: Nurses are required by law to cook meals for every patient
options.B: It generates extra revenue for the hospital administration
options.C: Proper nutrition is essential for preventing and managing chronic diseases
options.D: It replaces the need for administering prescribed medications

explanation: Good food is medicine! Helping patients get the right nutrients speeds up their healing and keeps chronic illnesses under control. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h8)

question: Why does waste material become hard and dry when it moves too slowly through the colon?

options.A: The liver stops producing mucus to lubricate the intestinal walls

options.C: Bacteria in the lower bowel multiply rapidly and dry out the waste
options.D: Extra time allows the colon to absorb more water than normal

explanation: Makes sense, right? If stool stays too long in the colon, the body keeps drawing out water, leaving the waste dry and tough to pass. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why do nurses apply a cotton stockinette and padding before wrapping the plaster rolls?

options.A: To add bright color and decoration to the finished cast
options.B: To help the wet plaster dry much faster from the inside
options.C: To protect the underlying skin from irritation and pressure
options.D: To prevent the limb from shrinking inside the hard cast

explanation: Padding acts as a cozy cushion between the hard plaster and bony areas, keeping the skin safe from sores. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the medical term when a baby is born without a fallopian tube?

options.A: Ovarian hypoplasia
options.B: Tubal agenesis
options.C: Uterine didelphys
options.D: Cervical stenosis

explanation: You've got this! 'Tubal agenesis' simply means the fallopian tube didn't form during development before birth. It's a great term to tuck away in your nursing notes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h1)

question: Which of these physical signs is often seen in healthcare workers dealing with the second victim experience?

options.A: Sudden loss of hearing
options.B: Uncontrolled involuntary tremors
options.C: Difficulty sleeping or insomnia
options.D: Complete temporary paralysis

explanation: Stress and trauma from clinical incidents can easily chase sleep away, leaving you tossing and turning at night. Recognizing these signs early helps you seek support fast! [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h2)

question: What makes record keeping an essential responsibility for a midwife working in the community?

options.A: It helps track birth rates, complications, and immunization coverage over time.
options.B: It replaces the need to talk directly with mothers during visits.
options.C: It is only required to satisfy strict hospital billing departments.
options.D: It prevents mothers from visiting traditional healers in the village.

explanation: Accurate community records allow midwives to monitor public health trends, catch missed vaccinations, and plan local health interventions effectively. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h2)

question: How do everyday nursing activities relate to research data?

options.A: Routine documentation and vital sign monitoring actively generate data
options.B: Clinical tasks are completely separate from any form of data collection
options.C: Nurses only encounter research data when publishing academic books
options.D: Research data is only collected by doctors in specialized laboratories

explanation: Every time a nurse records patient signs or care outcomes, they are contributing to the pool of clinical research data. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why can a severe, body-wide infection cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure?

options.A: The heart muscle suddenly stops beating with normal force
options.B: Widespread blood vessel dilation reduces systemic vascular resistance
options.C: The kidneys suddenly absorb all available fluid from the blood
options.D: Lungs take in too much oxygen and thin out the blood plasma

explanation: You got it! Severe inflammation makes blood vessels relax and widen all over the body, making it hard to keep blood pressure up. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h6)

question: A community health nurse wants to protect HIV-negative teens who are at high risk of exposure. Which preventive medication should the nurse discuss?

options.A: Emergency therapeutic surgical procedures
options.B: Intravenous antibiotic loading doses
options.C: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)
options.D: Immediate lifelong antiretroviral treatment

explanation: Spot on! PrEP involves taking daily anti-HIV medications to significantly lower the chances of catching the virus. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h8)

question: What happens when strategic, tactical, and operational plans fail to align in a hospital?

options.A: Long-term goals are achieved much faster
options.B: Daily nursing tasks become completely automated
options.C: Staff frustration increases and patient care suffers
options.D: The hospital automatically runs more efficiently

explanation: A disconnect between management levels creates confusion, wasted effort, and poor outcomes for patients. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the most important daily protection for a leprosy patient whose feet have lost feeling?

options.A: Soaking the feet in hot water daily to stimulate blood flow
options.B: Applying strong chemical antiseptics to unbroken skin daily
options.C: Wearing well-fitted, protective footwear at all times
options.D: Binding the toes tightly together to prevent accidental stubbing

explanation: Spot on! Since they can't feel pain, good shoes protect their soles from everyday cuts, stones, and ulcers. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h5)

question: In which zone of the surgical suite are hospital staff still allowed to wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Unrestricted zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Sterile core zone
options.D: Semi-restricted zone

explanation: The unrestricted zone is the front area where you enter and receive patients before changing into your fresh theatre scrubs. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h2)

question: Who chooses the Village Health Workers to serve in rural communities?

options.A: The federal minister of health
options.B: The community members themselves
options.C: International donor agencies
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Wonderful! When the community picks their own health worker, it builds instant trust and ensures the care fits their local culture. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h5)

question: You spot an infusion pump cord stretched tightly across a busy hospital walkway. What should you do right away?

options.A: Cover the cord with a wet towel to make it more visible
options.B: Leave it alone because pumps need power to stay functional
options.C: Unplug the pump and run it entirely on low battery power
options.D: Reroute the cord safely out of the walkway to prevent tripping

explanation: Cords across walkways are dangerous tripping hazards for staff and visitors. Moving it safely out of the way keeps everyone walking safely! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient starts having a psychomotor seizure while sitting on a chair in the ward. What should you do immediately?

options.A: Force a padded tongue depressor firmly between the teeth
options.B: Restrain the arms tightly to stop the automatic movements
options.C: Ease the patient to the floor and clear nearby hazardous objects
options.D: Leave the room immediately to call the attending physician

explanation: Patient safety is job number one! Guiding them gently to the floor prevents nasty falls and bumps against furniture. You're going to be an amazing ward nurse! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h7)

question: A toddler is showing growth faltering. What is the most practical nutrition advice to give the mother?

options.A: Stop all breastfeeding immediately and switch entirely to cow milk
options.B: Only feed the child imported baby cereals bought from supermarkets
options.C: Reduce the number of daily meals to allow the child's stomach to rest
options.D: Use available local food items to make nutrient-dense meals given more frequently

explanation: Keep advice practical! Recommend affordable, locally available foods that the family can easily prepare and feed the child more often. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h8)

question: What is the main job of a standard hearing aid?

options.A: To amplify surrounding sounds so the damaged ear can detect them
options.B: To convert spoken words directly into written text on a screen
options.C: To remove impacted earwax from deep inside the ear canal
options.D: To surgically replace the cochlea with an electronic processor

explanation: Exactly! Think of a hearing aid as a tiny personal amplifier that makes everyday sounds loud enough for the ear to pick up. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h4)

question: What happens to total maternal serum calcium levels during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: They decrease due to hemodilution and lower albumin
options.B: They increase significantly to support fetal bone growth
options.C: They remain completely unchanged throughout all trimesters
options.D: They drop dangerously low because of kidney failure

explanation: Total serum calcium drops because blood volume expands and blood protein levels fall, but ionized calcium stays normal. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary benefit of herd immunity in a community?

options.A: It replaces the need for personal hygiene and clean water
options.B: It completely eliminates all viruses from the global environment
options.C: It protects vulnerable individuals who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: It guarantees that natural infections never occur again

explanation: When enough people are immune, the chain of infection breaks, offering indirect protection to vulnerable, unvaccinated people. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of Cushing's triad when the brainstem is squeezed?

options.A: Irregular breathing patterns

options.C: Bradycardia
options.D: Widening pulse pressure

question: Your patient is nervous and shivering, and their ECG comes out looking super jagged. What should you do first?

options.A: Remove the chest electrodes and document that the test is impossible to perform
options.B: Immediately call the emergency response team for a suspected cardiac arrest
options.C: Apply extra conductive gel to the chest wall and increase the machine gain
options.D: Reassure the patient, provide a warm blanket to stop shivering, and repeat the tracing

question: Which vein is located in the antecubital fossa and is often used for emergency access or blood draws?

options.A: Digital dorsal vein

options.D: Great saphenous vein

question: A nurse wants to find the best evidence for managing pressure ulcers before updating the ward policy. What is the most appropriate first step?

options.A: Throw away all current textbooks and rewrite the guidelines from memory
options.B: Formulate a clear clinical question and search a nursing database
options.C: Wait for a pharmaceutical company to mail a new brochure
options.D: Ask every patient on the ward what treatment they prefer

question: A patient tests negative for an STI just three days after a risky exposure. What crucial advice must you give them?

options.A: Antibiotics should still be taken immediately to prevent future infections
options.B: No further precautions are necessary because the immune system has cleared it
options.C: The test may be a false negative due to the window period, so a repeat test is needed

question: Why is it a big mistake to force a patient to vomit after swallowing a corrosive chemical?

options.A: It forces the chemical to pass too quickly into the bloodstream
options.B: It neutralizes any antidote that medical staff plan to give later
options.C: It causes severe secondary chemical burns to the esophagus
options.D: It stops the liver from metabolizing the ingested poison

question: Why is the infant mortality rate considered a sensitive indicator of a community's general health status?

options.A: It shows the exact number of elderly people suffering from chronic heart conditions
options.B: It measures the total financial wealth of households in the region
options.C: It reflects the quality of maternal and child health services and living conditions

question: Why are blood thinners frequently given to patients admitted with moderate to severe COVID-19?

options.C: To thin the thick mucus secretions blocking the upper airways

question: Why can't we use standard adult BMI cutoffs to assess health risks in children and teenagers?

question: Which drug is commonly used first when a mother has postpartum hemorrhage from a soft uterus?

question: Where are immune cells primarily born and made in the body?

question: What is the main reason we use food guides in clinical and community nursing?

options.A: Controlling the market prices of agricultural crops
options.B: Ensuring every citizen eats the exact same calorie count
options.C: Translating nutrition science into practical meal advice

question: How do bacterial efflux pumps help germs beat drugs?

question: In reproductive health, what does the abbreviation mCPR stand for?

options.C: Monthly Clinical Patient Record
options.D: Maternal Child Protection Ratio

question: Why is cultural humility crucial for a community health nurse?

options.A: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build trust with community members

explanation: Understanding and respecting local traditions breaks down barriers and encourages people to accept health advice and services. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with end-stage kidney disease. Which sign is most directly linked to the kidneys losing their hormone-making job?

question: Which defense mechanism involves unconsciously pushing painful memories away so you don't have to think about them?

options.A: Repression

question: What is the primary benefit of using a blameless incident reporting system in a hospital?

question: What does a 'secondary' sexual dysfunction mean for a patient?

options.B: It occurs only during physical exercise

question: A nurse is accidentally poked by a needle from a patient who has Hepatitis B. Why is this exposure especially scary?

options.D: Hepatitis B can instantly destroy human skin cells on contact.

question: What is the primary characteristic of individuals who are placed in quarantine?

options.A: They are healthcare workers returning from a high-risk assignment.

options.C: They have laboratory-confirmed illness and active symptoms.
options.D: They refuse to take mandatory routine immunizations.

question: A mother visits the clinic with a four-month-old baby and asks about getting pregnant again immediately. What is your best nursing response regarding child health?

options.C: Encourage immediate conception so the children can grow up as close friends

question: Why does the tissue lining the urethra change from transitional cells near the bladder to tough squamous cells near the opening?

question: What happens to natural cortisol production when a patient takes high-dose steroids for a long time?

options.C: The brain stops signaling the adrenals to make natural cortisol
options.D: The pituitary gland increases natural cortisol production to compensate

explanation: Think of it like a thermostat: when there are already plenty of synthetic steroids floating around, the brain thinks, 'We have enough!' and tells the adrenals to take a break from making natural cortisol. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h1)

question: Which nursing action is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Checking blood pressure at a community health fair
options.B: Teaching foot care to a patient with diabetes

options.D: Administering a routine measles vaccine to a child

question: Which practice helps a disaster nurse stay strong and prevent burnout while responding to a crisis?

options.B: Ignoring personal feelings of sadness and pushing through work
options.C: Participating in regular peer support and debriefing sessions
options.D: Working continuous double shifts without taking meal breaks

question: What does the FIFO acronym stand for in food inventory management?

question: When is medication reconciliation most critical for a patient?

options.B: Only when the patient is discharged home

question: What is a core duty of a nurse-midwife in promoting safe motherhood?

options.A: Avoiding community engagement activities
options.B: Focusing exclusively on administrative paperwork
options.C: Providing respectful maternity care and screening during antenatal visits
options.D: Discouraging women from visiting modern hospitals

question: What does the abbreviation SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: Safety, Briefing, Assessment, Review
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Activity, Rate
options.D: System, Bedside, Action, Record

question: How does a stuffy, overheated lecture hall usually affect nursing students?

options.B: It improves their ability to memorize pharmacology lists
options.C: It sharpens their critical thinking and speeds up clinical math
options.D: It causes immediate hearing loss during lectures

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective nursing management planning?

options.A: Limited time due to busy daily duties

question: Why is it important for a primary health care nurse in a rural Nigerian community to understand seasonal disease patterns?

options.A: To accurately predict the winner of upcoming local political elections

question: What is the main job of the large intestine in our daily digestion?

question: Why are community sources like traditional healers or school registers important in rural disease surveillance?

options.B: Rural schools have better medical laboratories than city hospitals
options.C: Many rural residents may never visit a formal hospital when they first fall ill
options.D: Government health workers are forbidden from working outside cities

question: What direct action allows a muscle fiber to return to its normal resting length?
