question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in community health programs?

options.A: Monitoring deals only with finance, while evaluation deals only with drugs
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation assesses final outcomes
options.D: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously as activities are implemented, whereas evaluation measures the ultimate success or impact of the project at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which circumcision tool uses a small plastic ring tied over the foreskin that eventually falls off on its own?

options.A: Plastibell
options.B: Gomco clamp
options.C: Scalpel blade
options.D: Mogen clamp

explanation: That's the Plastibell! It stays snug on the tissue, cutting off blood supply to the extra skin so it drops off cleanly after a few days as it heals. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary job of the respiratory center in the medulla?

options.A: Filtering dust and germs out of inhaled air
options.B: Setting the basic rhythm and depth of breathing
options.C: Exchanging oxygen across the lung membranes
options.D: Producing mucus to keep the airway moist

explanation: The medullary respiratory center automatically drives the inhale-and-exhale cycle without needing conscious thought. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: What happens to blood vessels as a person ages normally?

options.A: Complete disappearance of capillary beds
options.B: Rapid dilation and excessive blood pooling
options.C: Spontaneous regeneration of damaged valves
options.D: Loss of elasticity and increased stiffness

explanation: You got it! Over time, blood vessels lose their stretchy fibers, becoming stiffer, which naturally contributes to higher blood pressure in older adults. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in the body?

options.A: Filtering metabolic waste products out of circulating blood plasma
options.B: Directing immediate, split-second muscle movements and reflexes
options.C: Coordinating slow, sustained processes like growth and metabolism
options.D: Producing physical barriers to protect internal organs from pathogens

explanation: While your nervous system handles quick reflexes (like pulling your hand from a hot stove), the endocrine system takes the long view—slowly and steadily managing things like your growth, mood, and metabolism. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which simple home modification helps prevent dangerous tripping hazards for someone using a walker?

options.A: Removing loose throw rugs from the floors
options.B: Adding decorative floor mats near doorways
options.C: Waxing hardwood floors until they shine
options.D: Placing heavy wooden furniture in hallways

explanation: Loose throw rugs easily bunch up under mobility aids like walkers and wheel tips, creating a major fall hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary mission of the National Senior Citizens Centre?

options.A: To build international airports for retired workers
options.B: To regulate bank interest rates for young adults
options.C: To manage primary school admissions in rural areas
options.D: To promote active aging and improve healthcare access for older adults

explanation: Correct! This center focuses specifically on looking after the social, health, and welfare needs of our elderly population. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h4)

question: What protective layers wrap around both the brain and the spinal cord?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Ventricles
options.C: Myelin sheaths
options.D: Synapses

explanation: The meninges are like sturdy cushion layers wrapped around your delicate central nervous system for safety. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why are patients with significant hearing loss also at a higher risk for accidental falls?

options.A: Hearing aids pull the head to one side and throw off normal body alignment
options.B: Inner ear structures involved in hearing also help control balance and spatial orientation
options.C: Patients with poor hearing refuse to wear shoes with proper non-slip soles
options.D: The medication used to treat hearing loss causes sudden daytime sleepiness

explanation: Spot on! The inner ear doesn't just handle hearing—it also houses our balance system. When there's an ear issue, balance can take a hit too. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is a major clinical benefit of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC) for teenagers?

options.A: They provide permanent sterilization after five years
options.B: They can be inserted independently by the user at home
options.C: They eliminate all risks of contracting viral STIs
options.D: They do not require daily compliance to remain effective

explanation: Once a LARC is placed by a clinician, it works quietly in the background for years without daily effort from the client. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why do women with very short menstrual cycles have a higher chance of developing endometriosis?

options.A: They cause the ovaries to produce abnormal thyroid hormones
options.B: They increase total lifetime exposure to menstruation and estrogen
options.C: They prevent the uterine lining from forming a thick functional layer
options.D: They cause immediate blockage of the cervical os during bleeding

explanation: More frequent periods mean more rounds of retrograde bleeding and hormone exposure over a lifetime, giving the condition more opportunities to develop. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T21#GNS216_U5_T21_h4)

question: Which of these best describes permanent harm?

options.A: A temporary drop in blood pressure after changing positions
options.B: A lasting disability or loss of function caused by an error
options.C: A mild headache that resolves after sleeping overnight
options.D: An allergic rash that disappears after taking an antihistamine

explanation: Permanent harm means the patient suffers a long-term or irreversible loss of ability. This is why our daily safety checks are so important. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why do nurses always stress taking birth control pills at the exact same time every single day?

options.A: It ensures the monthly period starts on a weekend
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of the medication pack
options.C: It maintains steady hormone levels in the bloodstream
options.D: It prevents the client from forgetting to eat meals

explanation: Consistency is key! Taking it at the same time keeps hormone levels steady so breakthrough ovulation doesn't sneak through. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h5)

question: A nurse researcher assigns hospital wards to receive a new handwashing training program by drawing lots. What experimental element is this?

options.A: Randomization
options.B: Manipulation
options.C: Data saturation
options.D: Blinding

explanation: Drawing lots means choice is left entirely to chance—that is classic randomization in action! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why must a nurse warm up a patient's cold hand before attaching a finger pulse oximeter probe?

options.A: Cold fingers have too much nail polish on them
options.B: Cold skin burns out the delicate infrared lights inside the sensor
options.C: Cold fingers prevent the patient from sitting still during the test
options.D: Cold temperatures cause vasoconstriction, reducing blood flow to the fingers

explanation: Poor peripheral circulation from coldness reduces pulse volume, making it hard for the machine to detect a clear signal. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which main chemical messenger in the brain do most sedative drugs target to slow things down?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Gamma-aminobutyric acid
options.C: Norepinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the body's natural brake pedal. Sedatives step on this pedal to help calm brain activity. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant patient asks how to reduce dark patches on her face. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Scrub the face vigorously with harsh soap twice a day
options.B: Stop drinking milk immediately to clear skin pigment
options.C: Apply strong bleaching creams prescribed over the counter
options.D: Apply daily sunscreen and wear wide-brimmed hats outdoors

explanation: Sunlight makes facial darkening (melasma) pop out more. Advising sun protection is a simple, effective tip every nursing student should know! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: Why is it important for nurses to figure out if a patient's worsening condition is from the disease or from medical care?

options.A: To prove that doctors are always responsible for clinical outcomes
options.B: To determine if the injury resulted from care management or the illness
options.C: To ensure the hospital avoids paying any financial compensation
options.D: To decide which patients need emergency psychological counseling

explanation: Exactly! We need to know if the problem came naturally from the illness or if something in our care caused it, so we can fix our processes and help the patient better. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h1)

question: What usually takes up the biggest slice of a nursing unit's operating budget?

options.A: Office stationery and printing
options.B: Patient dietary and meal trays
options.C: Staff salaries and labor costs
options.D: Building maintenance and paint

explanation: Nursing is all about people! Because healthcare relies so heavily on hands-on care, staff salaries and labor make up the highest cost in almost any unit. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h2)

question: As a nursing student, what major clinical risk should you watch out for in patients who lose skin sensation due to nerve damage?

options.A: Excessive sweating and dehydration
options.B: Rapid hair loss across the body
options.C: Loss of skin color pigmentation
options.D: Unrecognized injuries and chronic ulcers

explanation: Crucial nursing insight! If patients can't feel pain or pressure, they won't notice cuts, burns, or pressure sores, which can easily turn into dangerous ulcers if we don't protect them. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h7)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg normally take place in the female reproductive tract?

options.A: The interstitial segment
options.B: The isthmus
options.C: The ampulla
options.D: The fimbriae

explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle part of the fallopian tube where the sperm and egg usually meet. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h1)

question: Why do nurses use geometric dilution when mixing creams?

options.A: To ensure an even and thorough blend of the active drug
options.B: To remove all the natural oils from the base vehicle
options.C: To speed up the drying time of the lotion on the skin
options.D: To make the final mixture change color as it mixes

explanation: Mixing equal amounts gradually keeps the active drug from clumping up in one spot. It's a neat little trick of the trade! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h5)

question: A community nurse partners with local farmers and school headmasters to combat child malnutrition. Which concept does this action best demonstrate?

options.A: Private health insurance
options.B: Intersectoral linkages
options.C: Tertiary medical isolation
options.D: Acute hospital management

explanation: Partnering with agriculture and education sectors to address malnutrition is a classic example of intersectoral linkages. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: What does a sustainable elimination strategy primarily depend upon for long-term success?

options.A: Keeping all intervention data strictly secret from the public
options.B: Relying entirely on short-term foreign donor funding
options.C: Embedding prevention into national policies and health training
options.D: Punishing communities rather than engaging in dialogue

explanation: Sustainability means the work continues routinely through local systems, education, and government policy without fading away. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h8)

question: A woman receiving an oxytocin drip shows severe late decelerations on her CTG. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discontinue the oxytocin infusion immediately
options.B: Ask the mother to walk around the ward
options.C: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the pattern improves
options.D: Increase the oxytocin drip to speed up delivery

explanation: Stopping oxytocin removes the stimulus for contractions, giving the uterus a chance to rest and restore blood flow to the placenta. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h5)

question: What is the main focus of emergency nursing?

options.A: Providing long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Managing chronic lifestyle diseases at home
options.C: Conducting routine annual health screenings
options.D: Saving lives and stabilizing sudden illnesses

explanation: Emergency nurses specialize in immediate, acute interventions to stabilize patients facing life-threatening situations. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which finding during a community walkthrough survey indicates a high risk for vector-borne diseases like malaria?

options.A: Stagnant pools of water near residential houses
options.B: Concrete fences built around local market stalls
options.C: A high number of primary school children walking to class
options.D: Solar panels installed on community health center roofs

explanation: Mosquitoes that transmit malaria breed rapidly in standing water, making stagnant pools a major environmental health hazard. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a common everyday community stressor in our environment?

options.A: Living in a quiet, peaceful neighborhood
options.B: A balanced diet and regular exercise
options.C: Having too much free time and rest
options.D: Financial instability and high cost of living

explanation: Economic worries and the daily struggle to meet basic needs are massive sources of stress for many people around us. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why must a nurse sign or initial every entry made on a stock card?

options.A: To calculate the monthly salary bonus due to the nursing unit
options.B: To prevent the pharmacy department from reducing future supplies
options.C: To prove that the nurse worked extra hours on that specific day
options.D: To ensure accountability and provide a clear trail for audits

explanation: Signatures establish personal responsibility for every movement of stock, which is essential for investigating discrepancies later. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which local Nigerian vegetable is commonly used in soups to provide essential iron and vitamins for nursing mothers?

options.A: Raw cocoa powder
options.B: Refined white sugar
options.C: Ugu (fluted pumpkin leaves)
options.D: Dried cassava flakes

explanation: Ugu leaves are rich in iron and vital vitamins, making them a staple in local postpartum soups across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h6)

question: When checking over a recently bereaved female patient, what sign might make you suspect she went through harmful widowhood rites?

options.A: Unexplained scalp injuries and severe sudden weight loss
options.B: Expressed desire to join a local grief support counseling group
options.C: Requests for routine immunizations against common infections
options.D: A sudden increase in blood pressure readings during the visit

explanation: Rough hair shaving can hurt the scalp, and forced fasting often leads to quick, unhealthy weight loss. Good assessment skills catch these clues! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T10#GNS225_U6_T10_h5)

question: A nurse checks a patient's pedal pulses and finds the left pulse is strong while the right pulse cannot be felt at all. What is the most immediate clinical concern?

options.A: High blood pressure throughout the body
options.B: A potential blockage in the right leg artery
options.C: An allergic reaction to heart medication
options.D: A normal variation in elderly patients

explanation: An absent pulse on only one side strongly suggests local arterial occlusion or injury, requiring urgent follow-up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is a hollow-bore needle (like the ones used to draw blood) so dangerous if you accidentally prick yourself with it?

options.A: Hollow-bore needles often trap residual blood inside, increasing pathogen transfer
options.B: The plastic barrel attached to the needle releases toxic gas
options.C: Puncture wounds from needles never heal without surgical stitches
options.D: Needles used for drawing blood contain paralyzing chemicals

explanation: You nailed it. Because they are hollow, they act like tiny storage tubes carrying a good drop of infected blood right past your skin barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h3)

question: You want to improve child health in a rural village. What is the best first step?

options.A: Distribute standard vitamins without checking local diets
options.B: Ask local mothers about their main health concerns
options.C: Build a modern pediatric ward immediately
options.D: Report village leaders to the ministry of health

explanation: Brilliant! Talking directly to the community helps you understand their real challenges instead of just guessing what they need. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a gender stereotype?

options.A: Noting that anatomical differences affect drug metabolism
options.B: Assuming women are always more emotional than men
options.C: Recognizing that hormonal levels vary among individuals
options.D: Observing that height differs across global populations

explanation: Spot on! Assuming all women are emotional (or all men are cold) is a rigid stereotype rather than a fact. Everyone is unique! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a community diagnosis?

options.A: A laboratory test used to confirm typhoid fever
options.B: A prescription written for a patient with severe malaria
options.C: An official report written by the Minister of Health
options.D: An assessment of the overall health status of a population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at the health, living conditions, and resources of an entire group of people. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h4)

question: When is it ethically okay for a nurse to open a patient's electronic health record?

options.A: Whenever the patient is a personal friend or family member
options.B: Only when actively involved in that patient's direct clinical care
options.C: During routine breaks to pass the time between shifts
options.D: At any time to satisfy personal curiosity about a diagnosis

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred! You should only look at records for patients you are directly caring for as part of your duties. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is care in the emergency department prioritized based on severity instead of arrival time?

options.A: It is required by hospital administrative rules
options.B: Critically ill patients need immediate intervention to prevent death
options.C: First arrivals generally have minor complaints
options.D: Patients who arrive later usually pay higher fees

explanation: Triage ensures that those with life-threatening conditions receive immediate care regardless of when they walked through the door. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h1)

question: A student nurse organizes a session on safe waste disposal and clean water sources for a rural village. Which scope of health education does this fall under?

options.A: Maternal health
options.B: Curative medicine
options.C: Environmental health
options.D: Occupational health

explanation: Waste disposal, sanitation, and clean water are core components of environmental health education. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h4)

question: If a company tries to ship chemical waste abroad without telling the countries it passes through, what happens under the Basel Convention?

options.A: The company receives a warning but the shipment continues
options.B: The transit nations must accept the cargo if fees are paid
options.C: The shipment is illegal and prohibited from moving
options.D: The waste is automatically classified as non-hazardous

explanation: Exactly! Skipping the paperwork and failing to notify every country involved makes the shipment completely illegal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which group of patients is at the highest risk of accidentally breathing in (aspirating) barium during the test?

options.A: Patients with a history of high blood pressure
options.B: Patients with severe swallowing difficulties
options.C: Patients who receive a mild laxative post-test
options.D: Patients who fasted for longer than twelve hours

explanation: Good clinical thinking! If someone already struggles to swallow, they can easily choke and pull the barium down into their lungs. Always assess carefully! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h7)

question: If a displaced community is staying in a crowded makeshift camp after a flood, what health threat should the nurse expect next?

options.A: Immediate reduction in baseline community trauma rates
options.B: Rapid spread of waterborne and communicable diseases
options.C: Sudden widespread outbreaks of genetic blood disorders
options.D: Total elimination of chronic lifestyle health conditions

explanation: When people are crowded together with poor sanitation, infectious diseases can spread very quickly. Nurses play a huge role in preventing this! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h3)

question: A student just lists summaries of ten different articles back-to-back without linking them together. What is the main issue?

options.A: Forgetting to include the personal opinions of the patients
options.B: Using too many references from international nursing journals
options.C: Failing to synthesize and connect the themes across the articles
options.D: Writing the review before collecting any raw clinical data

explanation: A great literature review weaves studies together like a story, showing how they relate instead of reading like a random grocery list. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h4)

question: What is a common trap nurses should avoid when a patient starts a new drug and develops a weird symptom?

options.A: Checking the patient's blood pressure immediately
options.B: Assuming it is a new disease rather than a drug reaction
options.C: Notifying the doctor before the end of the shift
options.D: Asking the patient about herbal remedies they take

explanation: Don't rush to treat a drug side effect with a brand new disease diagnosis! Always check recent medications first. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient reports numbness in just one hand after a minor wrist injury. Which part of the nervous system is most likely involved?

options.A: Autonomic sympathetic system
options.B: Peripheral nervous system
options.C: Central nervous system
options.D: Cerebellar control center

explanation: Localized issues in a limb usually point to a peripheral nerve problem in that exact area. Brilliant deduction! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h8)

question: How do you know a health project has achieved sustainability?

options.A: The community can maintain the results and manage repairs without outside help
options.B: The foreign donors promise to keep sending money for the next ten years
options.C: The government takes over all financial responsibility for the village
options.D: The local nurse decides to stay in the village permanently

explanation: Sustainability means the local people have the skills, money, and will to keep the benefits going on their own. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h7)

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A legal termination performed in a fully equipped hospital
options.C: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor medical environments
options.D: Any abortion that requires the use of surgical instruments

explanation: You've got this! An abortion is unsafe if it's carried out by people without proper training or in places that lack basic medical standards. Keeping patients safe means knowing the difference. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h1)

question: Why might a teenager avoid visiting a local clinic for contraceptives even when the items are free?

options.A: The clinic only opens during midnight hours
options.B: Fear of being judged or seen by neighbors
options.C: Government rules forbid youth from walking outside
options.D: Contraceptives require a surgical procedure first

explanation: Stigma and lack of privacy in healthcare settings are major deterrents for young people seeking reproductive health services. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: A patient is suffering from severe diarrhea and vomiting. What condition are they most at risk for?

options.A: Fluid volume deficit
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Fluid volume excess

explanation: When fluids leave the body too fast from both ends, fluid volume drops quickly. That's why rehydration is usually the very first order of business! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h3)

question: What sign tells us a patient has reached clinical death?

options.A: Complete decay of all body cells
options.B: Cessation of breathing and heartbeat
options.C: Stiffening of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Total loss of liver and kidney function

explanation: You've got this! Clinical death simply means the heart and lungs have stopped working, so breathing and circulation completely halt. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h1)

question: How do early childhood attachment disruptions affect a person later in life?

options.A: They automatically cause physical brain damage within the first year
options.B: They can impair emotional regulation and increase vulnerability to stress
options.C: They guarantee that the person will develop schizophrenia as an adult
options.D: They prevent the individual from ever learning how to read or write

explanation: Unstable early relationships with caregivers can hinder a person's ability to trust others and manage intense emotions effectively as an adult. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is keeping an open posture and using friendly verbal cues so important in nursing care?

options.A: It ensures the physical examination takes less time to complete
options.B: It forces the patient to agree with the nurse's diagnosis
options.C: It prevents patients from asking questions about their medications
options.D: It builds rapport and encourages patients to share sensitive details

explanation: Correct! A welcoming body language creates a safe space where patients feel comfortable opening up about private worries. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which surfaces in a patient's room need cleaning and disinfecting the most often?

options.A: The outer walls of the hospital storage cupboard
options.B: High ceilings and ceiling fan blades
options.C: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and door handles
options.D: The lower baseboards near the floor corners

explanation: You're right! Bed rails and door handles are touched constantly by hands, so they collect germs the fastest. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic pale, dizzy, with a fast pulse and severe tummy pain after an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to return next week
options.B: Begin lengthy administrative registration before any medical action
options.C: Wait for laboratory blood test results before providing any fluids
options.D: Stabilize vital signs, start IV fluids, and prepare for emergency care

explanation: Pale skin, rapid pulse, and dizziness are warning signs of shock and hemorrhage. Your quick action with IV fluids and stabilization can save a life! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: What is the main goal of giving ovulation-stimulating medications like clomiphene citrate?

options.A: To thicken the uterine lining permanently
options.B: To clear blocked fallopian tubes
options.C: To increase male testosterone levels
options.D: To encourage the release of mature eggs

explanation: These helpful drugs nudge the ovaries to develop and release eggs when a woman's ovulation is irregular. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h4)

question: Why are hip and spine fractures very common in elderly patients with weakened bones?

options.A: These bones are made entirely of cartilage instead of bone.
options.B: These regions contain high amounts of fragile cancellous bone.
options.C: These bones are never protected by muscle tissue.
options.D: These areas never undergo normal bone remodeling.

explanation: Areas like the hip, wrist, and spine are packed with delicate cancellous (spongy) bone. When someone develops osteoporosis, these spongy areas lose their strength first, making them prime spots for fractures. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T3#GNS121_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is inhaling a chemical often more dangerous than getting it on your skin?

options.A: Rapid absorption into the bloodstream through the lungs
options.B: Localized swelling of the eye tissues
options.C: Delayed stomach ulceration and internal bleeding
options.D: Immediate burning of the outer skin layers

explanation: Think of the lungs as a massive highway into the body! Inhaled substances quickly cross into the tiny blood vessels (capillaries) in the lungs and travel straight to vital organs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which hormone is produced by the Leydig cells in the testes?

options.A: Testosterone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Great job! The Leydig cells are responsible for making testosterone, which is the main male sex hormone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h1)

question: A patient is recovering from deep skin wounds. Why is giving them extra protein so important?

options.A: To supply essential fatty acids for nerve insulation
options.B: To accelerate tissue regeneration and close wounds
options.C: To provide a quick surge of energy for walking
options.D: To prevent the kidneys from retaining too much fluid

explanation: Proteins are the body's chief repair crew. When there are wounds or burns to heal, the body needs extra protein to build new tissue and close the skin. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h3)

question: Which substance must be present in a rehydration solution to help activate the SGLT1 transporter in the gut?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Protein

explanation: Think of glucose as a helpful partner! It teams up with sodium to attach to the SGLT1 transporter, which helps pull both molecules into the intestinal cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h2)

question: Why do we use standard universal precautions for every single woman admitted to the labor ward?

options.A: Any patient can carry blood-borne infections even if their screening status is unknown
options.B: It saves time by eliminating the need to check laboratory test results
options.C: Pregnant women never develop secondary bacterial infections during birth
options.D: Government regulations only apply infection control to surgical patients

explanation: We treat all body fluids as infectious because in an emergency, we might not know a patient's status yet. Safety first for everyone! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: Which test checks the speed and strength of electrical signals in a peripheral nerve?

options.A: Lumbar puncture
options.B: Nerve Conduction Studies
options.C: Electromyography
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Nerve Conduction Studies use gentle, tiny electrical pulses on the skin to see how fast signals travel down the nerve highway. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h5)

question: Why must nurses be careful when reading antibody blood tests for an active infection?

options.A: Antibodies only work when the patient has a high fever
options.B: Antibodies can stick around in the blood long after an old infection is gone
options.C: Antibodies change shape daily inside the human bloodstream
options.D: Antibodies destroy the laboratory testing equipment if left too long

explanation: Well done! Because our immune system remembers past fights, a positive antibody test might just mean an old infection, not a current one. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is a key performance indicator used to evaluate directing effectiveness?

options.A: The physical color of the walls in the hospital ward
options.B: Medication error rates and patient satisfaction scores
options.C: The brand of uniforms worn by junior nursing staff
options.D: The total number of chairs in the nurse's lounge

explanation: Quality indicators like error rates and patient feedback directly reflect how well guidance and management are working on the floor. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h8)

question: What does the catchy phrase U=U mean in modern HIV care?

options.A: Urinary excretion of unabsorbed medication
options.B: Unprotected union under treatment
options.C: Universal use of universal precautions
options.D: Undetectable equals untransmittable

explanation: Brilliant! U=U means when a person's viral load is undetectable through ART, they cannot sexually pass the virus to others. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h3)

question: Which of these is a direct positive patient outcome linked to having highly motivated nurses?

options.A: Higher frequency of disciplinary hearings for junior staff
options.B: Increased total cost of medical supplies per admission
options.C: Faster turnaround times for hospital building construction
options.D: Lower rates of hospital-acquired infections and patient falls

explanation: When nurses are motivated and alert, they pay close attention to safety checks, which directly protects patients from preventable slips, falls, and infections. [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h7)

question: How is blood classified as a tissue in the human body?

options.A: Epithelial tissue
options.B: Nervous tissue
options.C: Muscular tissue
options.D: Connective tissue

explanation: You got this! Blood is a special type of connective tissue because it has living cells floating around in a fluid matrix called plasma. Think of it as a connecting transport system for the whole body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it helpful for a new nurse manager to see their administrative duties as making active choices?

options.A: It removes the need to consult senior staff
options.B: It speeds up the process of writing shift reports
options.C: It helps them take responsibility for outcomes
options.D: It guarantees that no mistakes will ever happen

explanation: When you accept that leadership is all about making choices, you can own the results, learn quickly from mistakes, and grow into a confident leader. [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is the briefing phase right before a scenario so important for students?

options.A: It gives students time to memorize a script for the patient interaction
options.B: It allows the instructor to test students on random trivia questions
options.C: It ensures that no student is ever allowed to make a clinical mistake
options.D: It establishes ground rules and helps create a safe psychological space

explanation: The briefing clarifies the rules, explains the environment, and reassures students so they feel comfortable participating without fear. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the most important check a nurse must do before starting any IV infusion?

options.A: Verifying the five rights of medication administration
options.B: Ensuring the patient fasts for at least 12 hours
options.C: Checking the patient's deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Obtaining a written surgical consent form from the doctor

explanation: Safety first! Always check the right patient, medication, dose, route, and time every single time before giving any drug. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h9)

question: A baby in Gallows traction has cool toes and a capillary refill of 4 seconds. What is your first step?

options.A: Notify the doctor right away
options.B: Put a warm blanket on their feet
options.C: Loosen the overhead ropes
options.D: Give extra pain meds

explanation: Cool toes and slow refill mean blood flow isn't reaching the foot properly. That's an urgent call to the doctor to protect the limb! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h3)

question: When assessing a postpartum mother at home, what does a firm uterine fundus indicate?

options.A: A delayed healing process of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: An abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity
options.C: Effective muscle contraction to prevent excessive bleeding
options.D: Complete closure of the cervix back to normal size

explanation: A firm uterus compresses open blood vessels at the placental site, which is vital for preventing postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the main focus of humanistic learning theory?

options.A: Computer-like processing speed and short-term memory limits
options.B: Observing role models in clinical hospital environments
options.C: The whole person, personal growth, and emotional well-being
options.D: Strict behavioral conditioning through rewards and punishments

explanation: Humanism cares about you as a complete human being—your feelings, your dreams, and your personal growth—not just your grades on a score sheet. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h5)

question: How do targeted drugs like rituximab help fight lymphoma cells?

options.A: By blocking all blood vessels feeding the tumor
options.B: By attaching to cell markers and flagging them for immune destruction
options.C: By replacing damaged DNA strands inside the cell
options.D: By telling the liver to make extra clotting factors

explanation: Targeted therapy acts like a smart missile. It sticks to a specific tag on the cancer cell so your immune system can spot and destroy it easily. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal of active case finding by a community health nurse?

options.A: Collecting accurate financial data for the local government health department
options.B: Reducing the number of patients who visit the clinic for minor headaches
options.C: Finding infected individuals early before they develop severe illness or spread the disease
options.D: Punishing families who refuse to bring their children for routine immunizations

explanation: Active case finding involves going into the community to identify sick people early, allowing prompt treatment and halting further transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h6)

question: A client comes to the clinic asking for a reversible method that lasts for several years without her needing to remember it daily. Which option fits best?

options.A: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking with her partner
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills taken every morning
options.C: An intrauterine device inserted into the uterine cavity
options.D: Male withdrawal practice during intercourse

explanation: Great choice! Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are long-acting and give continuous protection for years without needing daily action from the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h3)

question: Which bloodborne infection is most frequently caught through accidental needle-stick injuries?

options.A: Hepatitis B
options.B: Rotavirus
options.C: Rhinovirus
options.D: Influenza A

explanation: You're doing great. Hepatitis B spreads very easily through blood contact, making it a major occupational hazard when dealing with used needles. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: Which cancer is the most common among Nigerian women?

options.A: Liver cancer
options.B: Breast cancer
options.C: Cervical cancer
options.D: Ovarian cancer

explanation: Breast cancer is recorded as the leading malignancy among women in Nigeria and globally. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h2)

question: What should you tell a patient taking a sublingual medication?

options.A: Brush your teeth immediately before placing the tablet
options.B: Chew the tablet thoroughly and swallow with a large glass of water
options.C: Do not eat or drink until the tablet has completely dissolved
options.D: Swallow the tablet whole right after placement

explanation: Remind your patient to be patient! Eating, drinking, or talking can wash the pill away before it has a chance to soak into the mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T15#GNS125_U3_T15_h7)

question: Simply put, what is an antigen?

options.A: A protective protein made by B lymphocytes
options.B: A physical barrier found on human skin
options.C: A foreign substance that triggers an immune response
options.D: A type of white blood cell that eats bacteria

explanation: An antigen is basically any foreign tag or molecule on a germ that says 'intruder!' to your immune system, shouting for backup. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the standard baseline daily protein recommendation (RDA) for a healthy, less active adult?

options.A: 10 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.B: 5.0 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.C: 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.D: 2.5 grams per kilogram of body weight

explanation: 0.8 grams per kg is the golden baseline set to keep a healthy adult from deficiency and maintain a steady nitrogen balance. Easy to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h5)

question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding according to health guidelines?

options.A: First two weeks of life
options.B: Throughout the entire first year
options.C: First six months of life
options.D: Only until solid foods are desired at month two

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding provides all necessary nutrients and protective antibodies for the first six months of an infant's life. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)

question: What is an important safety action when caring for a patient who is actively having a tonic-clonic seizure?

options.A: Immediately give a large glass of water to prevent dehydration
options.B: Hold the patient's arms and legs tightly to stop all shaking
options.C: Keep emergency equipment like suction and oxygen close at hand
options.D: Force a padded wooden tongue depressor between the teeth

explanation: Safety first! Keeping suction and oxygen nearby helps you manage their airway once the shaking stops. Never try to hold their limbs down or force anything into their mouth. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h7)

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Spot on! Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles everywhere in the body, which is why digestion slows down and blood vessels change. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h2)

question: Why do nurses need to understand both the law and professional ethics?

options.A: To bypass the need for patient consent during emergencies
options.B: To avoid breaking the law while giving kind, respectful care
options.C: To ensure hospitals never face financial audits
options.D: To successfully prosecute patients who break hospital rules

explanation: Knowing both legal rules and ethical principles protects you from trouble while making sure your patients always feel respected and cared for! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: How does smoking affect the upper gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: It stops the liver from producing bile entirely
options.B: It relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, causing acid reflux
options.C: It increases the production of protective stomach mucus
options.D: It permanently closes the pyloric sphincter valve

explanation: Nicotine makes the muscular valve between your food pipe and stomach lazy, letting stomach acid slip backward and cause heartburn. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why is counting journal download numbers alone not enough to prove a study was clinically successful?

options.A: It does not show whether patient outcomes or clinical practices actually improved
options.B: It stops other researchers from ever citing the published paper again
options.C: It means the hospital administration will refuse to read the document
options.D: It proves that the research study contained major statistical calculation errors

explanation: Brilliant! Downloads show people are interested, but they don't guarantee the findings were actually used at the bedside to help patients. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h7)

question: A patient contracts a skin infection after touching a blood pressure cuff that was used on a previous infected patient without being cleaned. What type of transmission is this?

options.A: Common vehicle water transmission
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Airborne droplet nuclei transmission
options.D: Indirect contact transmission

explanation: Because the germ traveled from the first patient to the cuff and then to the second patient, it is indirect contact through a fomite. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: Why is equitable distribution of funds across urban and rural clinics important?

options.A: To prevent rural health collapse and ensure all citizens have access to basic care
options.B: To make sure city hospitals get all the newest vehicles
options.C: To reduce the number of nurses working in rural areas
options.D: To satisfy international organizations without helping patients

explanation: Fair funding stops the concentration of resources only in cities while villages suffer without medicines. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the top priority for a nurse caring for a patient right after surgery in the recovery room?

options.A: Obtaining the signed surgical consent form from the family
options.B: Assisting the surgeon with closing skin incisions in theater
options.C: Monitoring airway patency, breathing, and vital signs
options.D: Discussing long-term dietary changes for home care

explanation: Airway and breathing always come first! In recovery (PACU), keeping those airways clear and vitals stable is your number one life-saving duty. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which data collection method involves walking through the community to visually inspect environmental conditions?

options.A: Laboratory testing
options.B: Structured survey
options.C: Key informant interview
options.D: Observation

explanation: Observation or windshield surveys allow nurses to physically see housing conditions, water sources, and waste disposal practices. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why is monitoring serum albumin and prealbumin important for these patients?

options.A: They tell the doctor if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.B: They show whether the patient is drinking enough water every day
options.C: They help track the body's protein status and detect malnutrition early
options.D: They measure the exact amount of urine produced each hour

explanation: Blood protein levels give healthcare providers an objective look at how well the patient is tolerating the dietary restriction. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h5)

question: Why are traditional media like local drama and folk songs so effective in rural health education?

options.A: They replace the need for community health nurses entirely
options.B: They cost nothing to produce compared to printing posters and books
options.C: They are scientifically proven to kill infectious bacteria instantly
options.D: They are culturally familiar, entertaining, and work well even with low literacy

explanation: Music and drama speak straight to people's hearts and culture, making them brilliant tools even when community members can't read well. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h5)

question: How does nursing in the community differ from working in a big hospital ward?

options.A: Home nurses rely heavily on resourcefulness and critical thinking in the community.
options.B: Home nurses have direct access to immediate physician support at all times.
options.C: Hospital nurses perform fewer physical assessments than community nurses.
options.D: Hospital nurses manage fewer complex chronic conditions than home nurses.

explanation: You got it! Without hospital equipment and doctors right next door, home care nurses have to trust their training, think on their feet, and solve problems creatively. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is a virtual health community?

options.A: An online space where people connect for health support
options.B: A physical clinic equipped with virtual reality headsets
options.C: A government database of all registered nurses in a country
options.D: An emergency ambulance fitted with satellite navigation

explanation: You got it! Think of online support groups, health forums, and social media pages where people share health tips. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h7)

question: When we talk about a patient's sociocultural needs in nursing, what are we mainly looking at?

options.A: Shared beliefs, values, customs, and economic realities
options.B: Hospital administrative policies and room assignments
options.C: Strictly physical therapy exercises and mobility aids
options.D: Laboratory values and diagnostic imaging results

explanation: Spot on! Sociocultural needs are all about the human side of things—their culture, beliefs, and how they live day-to-day. It shapes how they view health! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h1)

question: You finish a neuro check and notice a brand new weakness in your patient's right arm. What should you do right away?

options.A: Discharge the patient home with instructions to rest
options.B: Wait until the end of your shift to write it in the chart
options.C: Report the finding immediately to the healthcare provider
options.D: Assume the patient is just tired and ignore the finding

explanation: You made the right call! Sudden neurological changes always need quick medical attention to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h8)

question: What is a major complication of untreated chlamydia or gonorrhea in young females?

options.A: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Elevated blood cholesterol
options.C: Chronic juvenile arthritis
options.D: Idiopathic hypertension

explanation: Well done! If lower tract infections are left untreated, they can travel upward and cause painful pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) and fertility issues. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h4)

question: A CHEW is treating a child with severe malaria who suddenly starts having seizures and won't respond. What should the worker do right away?

options.A: Ask a village volunteer to handle the case
options.B: Discharge the child home with instructions to rest
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled immunization clinic day
options.D: Initiate an immediate emergency referral to a higher-level facility

explanation: You're thinking like a true clinician! Seizures are a major emergency that a primary clinic can't handle alone, so rushing the child to a higher-level facility is a life-saving move. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which day hospital setup shares resources directly with a larger general or psychiatric hospital?

options.A: The virtual outreach model
options.B: The mobile crisis model
options.C: The standalone model
options.D: The integrated model

explanation: Well done! The integrated model is physically and administratively linked to a main hospital, sharing staff and facilities. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of using a clean delivery kit during a home birth?

options.A: To speed up the progress of the first stage of labor
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing by the birth attendant
options.C: To prevent infection for both mother and newborn
options.D: To provide entertainment for the family during labor

explanation: Simple and crucial—the kit provides clean, germ-free items to stop harmful bacteria from causing infections during and after birth. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main job of a fetoscope during labor?

options.A: To listen to the baby's heartbeat and check for distress
options.B: To check how wide the cervix has opened
options.C: To measure the warmth of the amniotic fluid
options.D: To listen to the mother's tummy sounds after birth

explanation: A fetoscope is your special window into how the baby is doing, helping you make sure the little one is handling contractions just fine. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which characteristic of an effective nursing plan allows it to adapt to sudden patient admissions?

options.A: Secrecy
options.B: Rigidity
options.C: Complexity
options.D: Flexibility

explanation: Healthcare changes constantly, so a plan must be flexible enough to bend when emergencies happen. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is physical therapy so important after breast cancer surgery?

options.A: To stimulate rapid hair growth after finishing chemotherapy sessions
options.B: To close surgical skin incisions faster without needing sutures
options.C: To reduce the patient's daily requirement for oral pain medication
options.D: To prevent shoulder stiffness and restore full movement of the arm

explanation: Chest and armpit surgery can make the shoulder freeze up. Gentle physiotherapy helps patients get their arm movement back completely. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h8)

question: What is the main safety perk of having a drug library built into a smart IV pump?

options.A: It alerts nurses when a dose falls outside safe clinical limits
options.B: It automatically orders new IV bags when fluid levels run low
options.C: It replaces the need to check patient IV insertion sites
options.D: It measures the exact urine output generated during the shift

explanation: You nailed it! The drug library acts like a safety checklist, warning you instantly if a programmed dose is too high or too low. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h3)

question: What does a psychoactive substance mainly do to the human body?

options.A: It permanently repairs damaged nerve tissues
options.B: It alters brain function and mental state
options.C: It lowers overall blood pressure immediately
options.D: It speeds up the process of digestion

explanation: Spot on! Psychoactive substances target the central nervous system, which changes how a person thinks, feels, and behaves. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h1)

question: What is a direct financial barrier to emergency obstetric care in poor communities?

options.A: Mandatory taxes on all pregnant women
options.B: Free distribution of essential obstetric medications
options.C: High transportation costs to reach the nearest health facility
options.D: Excessive availability of free community health centers

explanation: Lack of funds for transport often delays getting to the hospital during an obstetric emergency, worsening outcomes. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h2)

question: What long-term problem can happen to the urinary tract from severe scarring due to untreated infections?

options.A: Testicular hypertrophy
options.B: Urethral strictures
options.C: Enlarged prostate gland
options.D: Chronic kidney stones

explanation: When the urethra gets badly inflamed and heals with scar tissue, it narrows down (a stricture), making it tough to pee normally. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the main job of anti-spasmodic drugs in the tummy?

options.A: To coat the stomach lining and prevent acid ulcers
options.B: To kill harmful bacteria causing stomach infections
options.C: To speed up the transit time of stool in the colon
options.D: To relax overactive smooth muscle and relieve cramps

explanation: Think of anti-spasmodics as a calming massage for your gut muscles. They help stop those painful, tight cramps when the tummy muscles are working into overdrive! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h1)

question: What usually happens when a country struggles to collect enough domestic taxes for public services?

options.A: A sudden surplus of funds for hospital construction
options.B: Complete elimination of out-of-pocket patient fees
options.C: Immediate achievement of the Abuja Declaration target
options.D: Increased reliance on external grants and borrowing

explanation: When local tax revenue is low, governments often have to seek loans or donor grants to keep funding public sectors like healthcare. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why might a clinical protocol that works wonderfully in an adult surgical ward fail if copied directly into a children's ward?

options.A: Adult patients always recover faster than pediatric patients regardless of care
options.B: Surgical nurses have much higher educational degrees than pediatric nurses
options.C: Children's wards never use standard hospital protocols of any kind
options.D: Different units have unique patient needs, workflows, and environmental contexts

explanation: Every ward has its own unique vibe and patient needs! We always need to tweak a practice to fit the receiving unit rather than copy-pasting blindly. [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know about anti-discrimination policies in healthcare?

options.A: To replace hospital administrators in their daily jobs
options.B: To ensure only male patients receive specialized care
options.C: To guide and support patients who face unfair treatment
options.D: To avoid ever having to speak with patients about gender

explanation: Knowing patients' rights lets you stand up and advocate for them when they face unfair treatment in the clinic. You're well on your way to becoming a fantastic nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h9)

question: What do we call the number of staff members who report directly to a single manager?

options.A: Chain of command
options.B: Work specialisation
options.C: Span of control
options.D: Formalisation level

explanation: The 'span of control' simply refers to how many people a boss is directly in charge of guiding. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h2)

question: What action officially marks the start time of a 24-hour urine collection test?

options.A: Having the patient empty their bladder and discarding that urine
options.B: Drinking two large glasses of water right before the test starts
options.C: Saving the very first morning urine sample in the collection jug
options.D: Collecting all urine produced starting from midnight regardless of sleep

explanation: To get an accurate 24-hour count, we start with a totally empty bladder so we don't accidentally count old urine that sat in the body overnight! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h6)

question: What's the main difference between accounting and budgeting in healthcare?

options.A: Accounting is handled exclusively by nurses while budgeting is done by doctors.
options.B: Accounting focuses only on nursing salaries while budgeting tracks patient medications.
options.C: Accounting is a short-term daily task while budgeting is only done every ten years.
options.D: Accounting looks at past financial records while budgeting plans for future financial needs.

explanation: Think of accounting as looking in the rearview mirror at what you've already spent, while budgeting is looking through the windshield to plan what's ahead! [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h1)

question: Who should be involved when checking if an intersectoral health program was successful?

options.A: External foreign auditors exclusively
options.B: All participating sectors and community representatives
options.C: Private pharmaceutical company executives
options.D: Only the federal minister of health

explanation: Correct! Because many groups built the project together, everyone involved—including the community—needs a voice in evaluating how it went. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)

question: Why are children usually considered very vulnerable to emotional trauma during emergencies?

options.A: They recover faster than adults without any need for reassurance
options.B: They rarely notice when dangerous environmental events happen
options.C: They possess complete immunity to long-term anxiety disorders
options.D: They have limited emotional coping skills and rely heavily on adults

explanation: Exactly! Children are still learning how to process big emotions, so they depend greatly on calm, stable adults to help them feel safe during a crisis. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h3)

question: Why is performing FGM in a modern hospital still considered unacceptable?

options.A: It breaks medical ethics and human rights regardless of hygiene
options.B: It costs too much money for the local community
options.C: Hospitals lack the proper tools for cutting female genitalia
options.D: Modern medicine cannot stop the bleeding from FGM

explanation: A clean environment does not erase the severe physical and psychological trauma or the breach of medical ethics. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: What do we call a tumor that has traveled to the brain from another part of the body, like the lungs?

options.A: Benign tumor
options.B: Primary tumor
options.C: Metastatic tumor
options.D: Congenital tumor

explanation: You've got this! When cancer cells break away from a spot like the breast or lungs and travel to the brain, we call it a metastatic (or secondary) tumor. Think of it as a traveler from another part of the body. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h1)

question: What happens when a tumor suppressor gene experiences a loss-of-function mutation?

options.A: The cell immediately transforms into a benign fibrous cyst
options.B: The cell loses its molecular brakes and divides uncontrollably
options.C: The cell creates an outer capsule to prevent metastasis
options.D: Normal cellular division stops permanently in the G0 phase

explanation: Tumor suppressor genes normally slow down cell growth; losing them removes these protective brakes, allowing rapid tumor growth. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.D: To prevent harm to patients, healthcare workers, and the community

question: Why do patients with long-standing chronic pancreatitis eventually develop diabetes mellitus?

options.C: The liver stops responding to insulin because it is overworked by fat digestion.

question: Which PHC principle ensures that rural and underserved populations get a fair share of health services?

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable voices are heard equally during community meetings?

question: At what point in their journey can a cancer patient start receiving palliative care?

question: What prompted the creation of formal critical care nursing organizations and certification standards?

question: What is the job of the thermopile inside an infrared thermometer?

question: Why should a patient close their eyes during sensory testing?

question: What is the major danger of failing to treat puerperal sepsis promptly?
